nodes.name: ColorSpec
nodes.summary: Consumer-supplied color in any supported intake space, converted to [Oklch] during normalization. [Oklch] itself implements this interface, so round-trip specifications need no wrapper variant. The [Hex], [Argb], and [Hsl] constructors are lenient so resolution can report instead of crashing: values that cannot be interpreted (a hex string that does not parse, non-finite components) are rejected with a report entry, and out-of-range components are clamped.

nodes.name: IdentityIntent
nodes.summary: Brand-defining inputs: who the product is, independent of feel, influences, or floors. All fields are optional. [presence] is meaningful only when a brand color anchors it, and [supportingColors] act as secondary brand anchors. @property brandColor Primary brand color, in any supported intake color space. @property supportingColors Secondary brand anchors; at most three are honored and extras are rejected during normalization. @property presence How evident the brand color should be in semantic roles. `null` equivalents to [BrandPresence.Balanced]. @property typography Brand typeface intent, as candidates, role pins, or both. @property deriveColors When `true` (default), colors are synthesized from mood, brand, and domain signals. nodes.name: ComponentOverrides
nodes.summary: Per-component style patches keyed by component id. nodes.name: SpOnlyFontSizeDetector
nodes.summary: Reports a `Dp` value passed to a parameter that carries a font size. Basis requires every font size to be expressed in scale-independent pixels so that text responds to the user's OS-level font scale setting. A font size in dp is measured in physical units and stays the same size no matter how large the user has set their system font, which defeats the purpose of that setting for anyone using it to read more comfortably.

nodes.name: checkFontSizeArguments
nodes.summary: Reports every `Dp` argument bound to a font-size parameter of [node]. The argument-to-parameter mapping is computed by lint rather than read from call-site syntax, so named, positional and mixed calls are all covered. An unresolvable callee is skipped: without the signature there is nothing to indicate the argument is a font size.

nodes.name: isDpTyped
nodes.summary: True when [expression] evaluates to a `Dp`. `Dp` is a `@JvmInline value class`, so its type is erased: once `16.dp` has been unboxed for the call its expression type is the underlying `Float`, and a `Dp` produced by a constant or a function can arrive unboxed too. The call is therefore identified by the `dp` extension property in `androidx.compose.ui.unit` that produced the value, which survives unboxing and cannot be matched by any other expression yielding a `Dp`.

nodes.name: referencesDpExtension
nodes.summary: True when [expression] is, or ends in, a call to the `dp` extension property. The primary signal resolves the `dp` reference back to its declaration in `androidx.compose.ui.unit`. The fallback covers a `Float` receiver, where UAST does not always bind the extension: a property named `dp` on a number is unambiguous, and the receiver's type keeps the check from matching an unrelated `dp` member.

nodes.name: isDpDeclaration
nodes.summary: True when [expression] is a reference to a local or property already declared as a `Dp`. Value-class erasure leaves no use-site signal once a `Dp` has been given a name, so a declaration-typed reference returns false rather than guessing. Such a value is reported at its declaration instead, which keeps the diagnosis with the code that chose the unit.

nodes.name: isDpExtensionProperty
nodes.summary: True when [this] is the `dp` extension property declared in `androidx.compose.ui.unit`. UAST resolves a Kotlin extension property to the synthetic `getDp` accessor, so both the property name and its Java accessor form are matched.

tour.title: Project Overview & Architectural Conventions
tour.description: Explore AGENTS.md and settings.gradle.kts to understand the multi-module architecture (basis-theme, basis-components, basis-lint, demo-app), Kotlin standards, and public Basis prefix rules.

tour.title: Declarative Theme Intent
tour.description: Inspect BasisIntent and control models representing user-provided brand colors, mood, fonts, and granular scalar overrides.

tour.title: Deterministic Theme Resolution Engine
tour.description: Follow the resolve() pipeline in ResolutionPipeline.kt, ThemeDraft.kt, and stage processors (BaseStage, DeriveStage, ControlStage, EnforceStage).

tour.title: Color Science: Oklch Conversion & Gamut Mapping
tour.description: Understand perceptual color calculations, Oklch transformations, and contrast repair algorithms enforcing accessible, vibrant palettes.

tour.title: Design Tokens & Foundations
tour.description: Examine immutable token wrappers like DpValue, SpValue and the complete ResolvedTheme tree carrying color, motion, depth, radius, size, spacing, and typography tokens.

tour.title: Jetpack Compose Integration: BasisTheme & Ambients
tour.description: Inspect BasisTheme composable, LocalBasisTheme composition local, and ambient locals bridging resolved design tokens into idiomatic Jetpack Compose styling.

tour.title: Custom Lint Rules & Detekt Enforcement
tour.description: Explore Basis custom lint detectors ensuring proper font size usage (SpOnlyFontSizeDetector) and registry definitions.

tour.title: Pipeline Verification Test Suite
tour.description: Check the ResolvePipelineTest and unit test suites validating theme resolution, token conversions, and constraint assertions.

tour.title: Build Configuration & Convention Plugins
tour.description: Examine root build.gradle.kts and detekt.yml configuring strict zero-warning compilation and convention plugins across modules.
